Description: Experienced Heavy Forklift Operator (Concrete & Precast Loading)
Location: 77044

Schedule: Monday – Friday, 6:00 AM – 4:00 PM (Overtime / occasional Saturdays as needed)

Job Type: Full-Time

Pay: $22.00 per hour -DOE

Job Overview
We are seeking an experienced, safety-focused Heavy Forklift Operator to handle and load precast concrete products onto flatbed and specialty trailers. Because precast concrete is heavy, high-value, and prone to chipping or cracking if handled improperly, this role requires a skilled operator with proven experience maneuvering high-capacity forklifts in an outdoor yard environment.

Key Responsibilities
Operate high-capacity pneumatic forklifts (e.g., Taylor, Hyster, or similar heavy-duty yard equipment) to safely and accurately lift, transport, and load precast concrete products onto flatbed trailers.

Place dunnage, cribbing, and protective spacers properly between concrete pieces to prevent chipping, cracking, or load shifting during transit.

Verify product dimensions, piece counts, and shipping tickets against customer orders before and after loading.

Work closely with flatbed truck drivers and yard spotters to ensure proper weight distribution across axles and compliance with load-securement standards.

Stage finished precast products in the yard and keep loading lanes clear, organized, and safe.

Perform daily pre-shift inspections (hydraulics, mast, chains, forks, tires, and fluids) and report any mechanical issues immediately.

Communicate clearly with yard staff, supervisors, and truck drivers in both English and Spanish.

Required Qualifications
Experience: Minimum of [2–3+] years of proven experience operating heavy-capacity forklifts handling concrete, precast, pipe, stone, steel, or similar heavy industrial materials.

Language: Bilingual — fluent in both English and Spanish (verbal and basic reading comprehension).

Schedule Flexibility: Available to work Monday through Friday from 6:00 AM to 4:00 PM, with the flexibility to work occasional Saturdays as business needs require.

Transportation: Must have reliable personal transportation to and from the facility to ensure punctual 6:00 AM arrivals.

Certification & Testing: Valid forklift certification and the ability to pass a hands-on heavy-equipment practical evaluation on site.

Physical & Environmental Requirements: Comfortable working outdoors year-round in varying weather conditions, climbing on and off heavy equipment safely, and lifting/placing heavy dunnage up to [50–75] lbs.

Preferred Qualifications
Experience with specialized attachments (fork positioners, side-shifters, pipe clamps, or spreader bars).

Familiarity with DOT flatbed weight distribution and tie-down/securement requirements.

Position Summary
We are seeking a dependable, detail-oriented Trucking Dispatcher with experience managing the dispatch process from start to finish. The ideal candidate understands the demands of over-the-road (OTR) trucking and can effectively coordinate loads, drivers, dispatchers, and transportation management systems to ensure smooth and efficient operations.

This role requires strong communication, organization, problem-solving skills, and the ability to manage multiple time-sensitive tasks while maintaining accurate information across all company systems.

Key Responsibilities
Load Sourcing and Booking: Assist with finding available loads, confirming load details, and finalizing bookings.
TMS Data Entry: Enter, update, and maintain accurate load information in our Transportation Management System (TMS-EZ).
Driver Coordination: Communicate with drivers regarding load assignments, pickup and delivery schedules, progress updates, delays, and operational issues.
Team Coordination: Work closely with other dispatchers to ensure smooth communication, effective handoffs, and consistent operational coverage.
Data Accuracy and Reconciliation: Verify that load details, schedules, documentation, and other relevant information match across all systems used by the company.
Load Tracking and Monitoring: Monitor active loads, follow up on delivery progress, and help resolve issues as they arise.
Problem Resolution: Respond promptly to unexpected changes, delays, and other challenges that may affect drivers or load schedules.
Communication and Documentation: Maintain timely communication with drivers, brokers, fellow dispatchers, and other relevant parties while keeping records complete and accurate.
Schedule and Hybrid Work Arrangement
The position offers a hybrid work arrangement, combining in-office and remote work.

Standard hours: 7:30 AM – 4:00 PM.
Office attendance: A minimum of three days per week in the office is expected, with the remaining workdays performed remotely, depending on operational requirements.
Schedule transition: We are transitioning from a combination of day and night dispatching to a daytime-focused schedule for a temporary period. The duration of this transition has not yet been determined.
Schedule flexibility: Candidates must be comfortable with potential scheduling adjustments as business needs and dispatch coverage requirements evolve.
Important: OTR Operations Require 24/7 Coverage
Over-the-road trucking is a 24-hour-a-day, seven-day-a-week operation. Trucks may be moving at any hour, and delays, breakdowns, delivery changes, and other unexpected situations can arise outside standard business hours.

A 24/7 operational coverage requirement is non-negotiable. Candidates must understand the demands of OTR dispatching and be prepared to meet the after-hours, weekend, holiday, or rotating coverage expectations established for this position.

Although the standard daytime hours are 7:30 AM to 4:00 PM, these hours do not eliminate the need for continuous dispatch coverage while trucks are operating. Specific scheduling and coverage arrangements will be discussed during the hiring process.

Qualifications
Previous trucking dispatch experience, preferably in OTR operations.
Understanding of the dispatch process, including load sourcing, booking, driver coordination, tracking, and delivery follow-up.
Experience with a Transportation Management System (TMS); TMS-EZ experience is a plus.
Strong attention to detail and the ability to maintain accurate records across multiple systems.
Excellent communication and coordination skills.
Ability to prioritize tasks, manage competing demands, and resolve time-sensitive issues.
Reliable, organized, accountable, and capable of working independently in a hybrid environment.
Willingness to adapt to changing schedules and meet established OTR coverage requirements.
What Success Looks Like
The successful candidate will help keep loads moving efficiently, ensure drivers and dispatchers remain informed, maintain accurate information across all systems, and support reliable coverage throughout the dispatch process.

We are looking for someone who takes ownership of their responsibilities, communicates proactively, follows through on tasks, and understands that accuracy and reliability are essential in trucking operations.

If you have hands-on OTR dispatch experience and are comfortable working in a fast-paced, 24/7 industry, we encourage you to apply.

One important point to settle before publishing: Does “24/7, no exemptions” mean the dispatcher personally must be available around the clock, or that the dispatch team must maintain continuous coverage through scheduled shifts and handoffs? Those are very different job expectations. Clarifying this will help attract candidates who are a good fit and avoid misunderstandings about the 7:30 AM–4:00 PM schedule.
